zh.title: 40岁，我不再急着证明自己：一个设计师用 AI 做了 7 个产品，也重新学习怎样生活
zh.excerpt: 从大厂设计师、连续创业与人生低谷，到重新回到设计职场、AI 与独立创作。
zh.content:
![向内认识自己，向外如水而行](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-01.jpg)

有很长一段时间，我的人生都在做同一件事：

> 证明自己。

证明自己足够优秀，证明自己能创业成功，证明自己可以挣大钱，证明即使经历过很多失去，我仍然能够重新站起来。

现在40岁了，我反而越来越不想证明什么。

我更想做的是另一件事：

> 认识自己，接纳自己，成为自己，然后把它真正活出来。

去年，我重新回到了阔别已久的设计职场，又开始重新大量使用 AI；白天在公司做品牌与视觉，晚上做一些自己真正感兴趣的产品。

它们现在都被放进了一个属于我的小小世界：

> WonderElian.com

我越来越觉得，它们看起来完全不同，底层其实是在做同一件事：

> 把复杂的事物，重新变得清楚而有品味。

## CHAPTER 01｜35岁以前，我一直在向外证明自己

我是永歌，英文名 Elian。

湖南湘潭人，后来从北京回到了湖北武汉。

9岁因为一次意外，我经历了严重毁容，此后很多年陆续接受了30多次手术。

那段经历很早就让我意识到：人与世界之间，存在一个非常重要的东西——美。

小学四年级开始学习美术，后来我进入华中科技大学，学习工业设计与建筑，并继续攻读设计艺术学硕士。

毕业后加入美团，做品牌与 UI 设计。

那时候的我很相信一件事：

> 只要足够努力，就应该不断往上走。

更好的学校、更好的公司、更大的项目、更高的收入、更大的房子。

这些东西曾经构成了我对“成功”的理解。

后来，我开始创业。

做过 O2O，也做过区块链，以及抑郁症项目。

经历过大笔融资，也经历过项目归零。

在那些年里，我获得过很多东西，也失去过很多东西。

但真正影响我的，并不是哪一次商业上的失败。

而是我逐渐发现：

> 如果一个人永远需要依靠外部结果确认自己的价值，那么无论得到多少，他都很难真正安定下来。

![松手之后，路才重新出现](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-02.jpg)

## CHAPTER 02｜35岁以后，我的人生开始失去原来的坐标

人生后来进入了又一段很长的低谷。

事业和家庭上的巨变、身体和心理状态，以及对未来迷茫（绝望），一起出现。

过去那套“不断往前冲”的方法，突然失效了。

我开始第一次认真面对一些以前从来没有时间回答的问题：

> 我为什么这么怕失败？

> 如果没有职位、收入、项目和别人对我的评价，我是谁？

> 我到底是在过自己的生活，还是一直在努力成为别人眼里的“正确答案”？

过去我总觉得人生的问题需要被“解决”。

后来才慢慢发现，有些东西不是用来解决的。

而是需要被看见、被理解、被接纳。

我开始重新读《道德经》。

不是为了变成某种导师，也不是为了找到一个终极答案。

只是想弄明白：

> 如何活出自己，以及一个人究竟怎样才能与自己与世界相处？

## CHAPTER 03｜40岁，我重新回到了设计职场

现在，我在海外一家激光雕刻机公司从事设计工作。

我的工作从视觉设计慢慢延伸到品牌设计、官网、广告、宣传册、展会视觉以及产品表达。

这份工作让我重新认识了设计。

以前我经常把设计理解为：

> 把东西做得更好看，让用户体验更好。

现在我更愿意把它理解为：

> 把复杂的东西重新组织，让别人更容易理解、相信并愿意接近它。

一台工业机器有很多参数、技术和卖点。

但用户真正看到的，只是几秒钟。

品牌设计要做的，是把这些复杂的信息重新翻译：

什么最重要？

应该先说什么？

什么应该被看见？

技术如何转化成价值？

一台原本冰冷的设备，怎样变成一个有力量、有性格、值得相信的品牌？

这件事情我做得越久，越意识到：

> 设计可能一直都是我的那个“1”。

职业会变化。

工具会变化。

AI 会变化。

但我真正喜欢的事情似乎一直没有变：

发现问题，建立秩序，整理信息，然后把它重新表达得清楚、美，而且有感觉。

![让想法从混沌走向可以被使用的形状](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-03.jpg)

## CHAPTER 04｜AI 没有让我离开设计，反而让我重新爱上创造

从 ChatGPT 3.5、生成式 AI、Agent（Codex）出现以后，我几乎第一时间开始大量尝试。

图像、视频、文字、代码、产品、自动化……

以前一个设计师想做一款完整产品，需要程序员、产品经理、运营和大量资源。

今天，一个人可以完成的事情突然变多了。

这对我来说是一件非常兴奋的事情。

因为 AI 最吸引我的地方，并不是“省时间”。

而是它把一个人从：

> 我只能做自己会做的东西（环节）

带到了：

> 我终于可以把脑子里的东西真正做出来。

于是，下班以后，我开始做很多看起来没有什么关系的小产品。

慢慢地，它们变成了 WonderElian。

![不同的产品，来自同一套内在方法](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-04.jpg)

## CHAPTER 05｜WonderElian：把兴趣变成一个个真实存在的东西

WonderElian 不是一家创业公司。

至少现在不是。

它也不是一个为了证明“我会多少东西”而建立的作品集。

我更愿意把它理解成：

> Elian 的个人创作世界。

这里放着我最近做的设计，也放着最近借助 AI 做出来的一些独立产品（会持续迭代）。

### 一休冥想 YIXIU

这是一个关于冥想、呼吸、声音与安静的产品。

它来自我自己走过低谷以后一个越来越简单的认识：

> 苟着，先照顾身体，安顿情绪，再继续前行。

我们总想立刻解决人生的问题。

但很多时候，一个人真正需要的可能只是先停下来，好好呼吸，睡一觉，让身体重新恢复一点力量。

### 不二 · 认识自己

这是我最近做的人类图产品。

我并不把人类图当作科学结论，也不认为一个系统可以告诉任何人“你应该成为谁”。

我真正感兴趣的是：

> 我们还可以通过哪些角度观察自己？我们的人生使用说明书（出厂设置）是什么样子？顺着它来活会不会舒服一些？

有时候，一个新的视角并不会直接给出答案。

但它会让我们提出一个以前没有认真想过的问题。

而认识自己，往往就是从一个好问题开始。

### 三慢问道 WENDAO

这是一个重新阅读《道德经》的产品。

我尝试用现代的信息设计、视觉和 AI，把这些已经存在两千多年的文字重新整理，让它离今天的普通人近一点。我尤其喜欢“对我们的启发”。

在做这个产品的过程中，我也慢慢总结出了自己现在很喜欢的四个词：

> 一休、不二、三慢、如水。

一休，是先照顾身体，也照顾情绪。

不二，是接受人生既有高峰，也有低谷。

三慢，是慢下来、慢慢来、慢慢成为。

如水，是不固执于某一种身份，而是在变化中保持自己的内核。

最后它们汇成一句话：

> 向内认识自己，向外如水而行。

### 虾子曰 · 昨日世界

我一直对这个世界保持着很强的好奇心。

AI、科技、商业、文化、体育、设计……

每天都有大量事情发生。

但我们真正缺少的，很多时候不是更多信息，而是：

> 做减法，挑选最热的8条信息，视觉呈现这些事情到底意味着什么。

于是有了“虾子曰”。

它尝试把每天发生的世界热点，重新整理成清楚、有观点、有画面的内容。

这里面既有内容，也有设计，还有我对这个世界持续的观察。

### Style Atlas · 艺术风格图鉴

这是一个关于视觉风格、艺术与设计学习，帮助大众提升审美的产品。

做了很多年设计以后，我越来越觉得真正重要的并不是记住多少风格名称，而是训练一种能力：

> 看见。

为什么这个画面舒服？

为什么那个构图有力量？

颜色、比例、节奏、留白和视觉重心究竟发生了什么？

很多所谓“审美”，其实并不是神秘天赋。

它可以被看见、被拆解，也可以慢慢训练。

### 品牌与增长设计

WonderElian 里也放着我的职业作品。

因为我并不想把“工作”和“个人创造”对立起来。

这是我现在最真实的设计训练场。

品牌策略、官网、宣传册、广告、展会、产品视觉……

这些项目让我每天都在真实商业环境中面对一个问题：

> 设计怎样真正帮助一个产品被理解、被信任和被选择？

它也是我从“视觉设计师”向“品牌设计”不断靠近的过程。

### WonderElian OPS

做的东西越来越多以后，又出现了一个新的问题：

> 怎样管理和运营它们？

项目、数据、内容、实验、运营、想法和下一步行动开始散落在不同地方。

于是我又给自己做了一个 AI 自动化运营系统。

它并不是为了把生活变成 KPI。

恰恰相反。

我希望把重复、琐碎和可以自动化的事情交给系统，让自己留下更多时间去做真正需要判断、审美和创造力的事。

这也是我现在理解 AI 的方式：

> 不是让人变得更像机器，而是让机器承担更多机器应该做的事情。

![看似分散的方向，正在汇成一条河流](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-05.jpg)

## CHAPTER 06｜这些东西看起来很散，其实一直是同一件事

有时朋友会问：

> 你到底在做什么？

冥想、人类图、《道德经》、艺术风格、工业品牌、AI 系统……

是不是太散了？

以前我也会焦虑。

总觉得一个人必须有一个非常清晰的标签：

设计师。

创业者。

AI 创作者。

产品经理。

博主。

后来慢慢发现，也许不需要。

因为这些东西的题材虽然不同，但我处理它们的方式高度相似。

面对一台工业机器，我会想怎样把复杂技术重新讲清楚。

面对《道德经》，我会想怎样让古老文字重新进入现代人的生活。

面对人类图，我会想怎样把一个复杂系统整理成普通人能够理解的视觉结构。

面对新闻，我会想怎样从巨大信息流里找到最值得看见的东西。

面对艺术，我会想怎样把模糊的“感觉”整理成可以学习的视觉语言。

所以现在如果一定要给自己找一个共同点，我大概会说：

> 我喜欢把复杂、抽象或冰冷的事物重新组织，用设计、AI 与产品，让它们变得清楚、美、有温度。

设计，是我的语言。

AI，是新的工具。

产品，是让想法真正存在的方式。

而好奇心，大概是这一切背后的动力。

## CHAPTER 07｜我仍然会焦虑，只是不再急着给人生一个答案

40岁并没有让我突然变得十分通透。

我仍然有工作压力。

有房贷。

有孩子。

也会担心未来。

也会想，如果有一天工作没有了怎么办？

看到别人创业成功，也还是会产生羡慕。

AI 发展得越来越快，也会担心自己的能力会不会有一天变得不再重要。

这些问题一个都没有消失。

真正变化的是：

> 我不再要求自己今天就把未来十年想清楚。

过去，一焦虑我就想赶紧找到“第二曲线”。

现在我更愿意把目前的工作做好，把品牌设计做深，同时利用晚上和周末，把真正有回应的想法一个个做出来。

不急着把每一样东西立刻变现。

但也不只是漫无目的地玩。

每做一个产品，我都希望留下点什么：

一个作品。

一个方法。

一种新的能力。

一段真实体验。

或者只是对自己更深一点的理解。

慢慢来。

看看这些东西最终会把我带到哪里。

## CHAPTER 08｜从“证明自己”，到“成为自己”

如果让我重新总结人生前四十年，我可能会分成两个阶段。

前半段，我一直在学习：

> 怎样成为一个更厉害的人。

后半段，我更想学习：

> 怎样成为我自己。

这并不意味着放弃努力。

也不是躺平。

恰恰相反，我还是每天做设计、玩 AI、做产品、工作、养家，也还是希望获得更好的收入和更多选择。

只是努力背后的动力开始发生变化。

以前是：

> 我要证明我可以。

现在更像：

> 这件事情我真的想做，所以我想把它做好。

这两者看起来很像。

身体的感受却完全不同。

![不必完整，也可以继续向前](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-06.jpg)

## CHAPTER 09｜WonderElian，也许会陪我很久

我不知道 WonderElian 最后会变成什么。

也许只是一个个人网站。

也许某些产品会慢慢长大。

也许未来会出现现在完全想不到的东西。

这都没有关系。

我希望它始终保留一点“Wonder”。

好奇。

惊喜。

奇迹。

对世界还有兴趣。

也还愿意做东西。

Elian 这个英文名，对我有一个很私人的意义：

> 我希望自己能够“活成一道光”。

年轻的时候，我理解的光可能是耀眼，是成功，是被很多人看见。

现在，我对它的理解变了。

光不一定需要很亮。

它也可以只是：

认真做好一件东西。

在别人需要的时候提供一点帮助。

把复杂的事情讲清楚。

对家人好一点。

对自己也好一点。

经历过黑暗以后，仍然愿意相信生活里存在美。

所以现在的 WonderElian，没有一个宏大的终极使命。

它只是记录一个40岁的设计师，如何继续用设计理解世界，用 AI 做一些自己真正感兴趣的东西，也重新学习怎样生活。

> 向内认识自己。
向外如水而行。
然后，慢慢成为自己。

![Elian 永歌](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-07.png)

en.title: At 40, I No Longer Rush to Prove Myself: A Designer Built Seven Products with AI—and Learned How to Live Again
en.excerpt: From big-tech design, serial entrepreneurship, and a long personal low to returning to design, AI, and independent creation.
en.content:
![Know yourself within. Move like water through the world.](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-01.jpg)

For a long time, my life seemed to revolve around one thing:

> Proving myself.

Proving that I was good enough, that I could build a successful company, that I could make a lot of money, and that even after losing so much, I could still stand up again.

Now that I am 40, I feel less and less inclined to prove anything.

I want to do something else instead:

> Know myself, accept myself, become myself—and then truly live it.

Last year, I returned to the design profession after a long time away and began working intensively with AI again. By day, I work on brand and visual design at a company. At night, I make products that genuinely interest me.

They now live together in a small world of my own:

> WonderElian.com

The more I look at them, the more I realize that although they appear completely different, they are all doing the same thing underneath:

> Making complex things clear and tasteful again.

## CHAPTER 01｜Before 35, I Was Always Proving Myself to the Outside World

My name is Yongge, and my English name is Elian.

I grew up in Xiangtan, Hunan. After living in Beijing, I eventually returned to Wuhan, Hubei.

At nine, an accident severely disfigured me. Over the years that followed, I underwent more than thirty operations.

That experience made me aware, very early, of something deeply important between people and the world: beauty.

I began studying art in fourth grade. Later, I entered Huazhong University of Science and Technology to study industrial design and architecture, then continued with a master's degree in design arts.

After graduating, I joined Meituan as a brand and UI designer.

At the time, I believed one thing very strongly:

> If you work hard enough, you should always keep moving upward.

A better school, a better company, bigger projects, a higher income, a larger home.

These things once formed my definition of “success.”

Later, I began starting companies.

I worked on O2O, blockchain, and a project related to depression.

I experienced large rounds of funding—and projects falling all the way back to zero.

In those years, I gained many things and lost many things.

But what affected me most was not any particular business failure.

It was the realization that:

> If you always need external results to confirm your worth, no matter how much you gain, you will find it difficult to become truly settled.

![Only after letting go did the road appear again.](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-02.jpg)

## CHAPTER 02｜After 35, My Life Lost Its Old Coordinates

Life then entered another long low period.

Major changes in work and family, struggles in both body and mind, and confusion—even despair—about the future all arrived at once.

The old method of “keep charging forward” suddenly stopped working.

For the first time, I began to face questions I had never made time to answer:

> Why am I so afraid of failure?

> Without a title, income, projects, or other people's judgments, who am I?

> Am I living my own life, or merely trying to become the “right answer” in other people's eyes?

I used to think life's problems had to be “solved.”

Only gradually did I understand that some things are not there to be solved.

They need to be seen, understood, and accepted.

I began reading the Tao Te Ching again.

Not to become a teacher, and not to find an ultimate answer.

I simply wanted to understand:

> How do I live as myself, and how can a person truly live with both self and world?

## CHAPTER 03｜At 40, I Returned to the Design Profession

Today, I work as a designer at an international laser-engraving company.

My work has gradually expanded from visual design into branding, websites, advertising, brochures, exhibition graphics, and product communication.

This work introduced me to design all over again.

I used to think of design as:

> Making things look better and improving the user experience.

Now I would rather define it as:

> Reorganizing complexity so people can understand it, believe in it, and feel willing to approach it.

An industrial machine contains many parameters, technologies, and selling points.

But the user may only look at it for a few seconds.

The job of brand design is to translate all that complexity:

What matters most?

What should be said first?

What needs to be seen?

How does technology become value?

How can a cold machine become a powerful, distinctive, trustworthy brand?

The longer I do this work, the more I realize:

> Design may always have been my “one.”

Careers change.

Tools change.

AI changes.

But what I truly enjoy has barely changed at all:

Finding problems, creating order, organizing information, and expressing it again with clarity, beauty, and feeling.

![Giving an idea a form that can be used.](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-03.jpg)

## CHAPTER 04｜AI Did Not Pull Me Away from Design. It Made Me Love Creating Again

When ChatGPT 3.5, generative AI, and agents such as Codex appeared, I began experimenting almost immediately.

Images, video, writing, code, products, automation…

In the past, a designer who wanted to make a complete product needed engineers, product managers, operators, and a great deal of resources.

Today, what one person can complete has expanded dramatically.

For me, that is thrilling.

What draws me to AI is not simply “saving time.”

It moves a person from:

> I can only do the parts I already know how to do

to:

> I can finally make what is in my head real.

So after work, I began making many small products that seemed unrelated.

Little by little, they became WonderElian.

![Different products, one inner method.](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-04.jpg)

## CHAPTER 05｜WonderElian: Turning Interests into Things That Really Exist

WonderElian is not a startup.

At least, not now.

Nor is it a portfolio built to prove “how many things I can do.”

I prefer to think of it as:

> Elian's personal world of making.

It holds my recent design work and a collection of independent products I have made with AI—products that will keep evolving.

### Yixiu Meditation

This is a product about meditation, breathing, sound, and quiet.

It grew from a simple understanding that became clearer after my own low period:

> Hold on. First care for the body, settle the emotions, and then continue.

We always want to solve life's problems immediately.

But often what a person really needs is to pause, breathe deeply, sleep, and let the body recover a little strength.

### Bu'er · Know Yourself

This is the Human Design product I made recently.

I do not treat Human Design as a scientific conclusion, nor do I believe any system can tell someone “who you should become.”

What genuinely interests me is:

> From what other angles can we observe ourselves? What might our personal operating manual—our factory settings—look like? Would life feel easier if we moved with them?

A new perspective does not always provide an answer.

But it may help us ask a question we have never seriously considered.

And knowing yourself often begins with a good question.

### Wendao · The Slow Way

This is a product for reading the Tao Te Ching anew.

I use modern information design, visuals, and AI to reorganize words written more than two thousand years ago, bringing them closer to people living today. I especially enjoy exploring “what this can teach us now.”

While making it, I gradually arrived at four phrases that matter deeply to me:

> Yixiu, Bu'er, Sanman, Rushui—rest, wholeness, slowness, and water.

Yixiu means caring for the body and the emotions first.

Bu'er means accepting that life contains both peaks and valleys.

Sanman means slowing down, taking your time, and becoming little by little.

Rushui means not clinging to a fixed identity, but preserving your core through change.

Together, they become one sentence:

> Know yourself within. Move like water through the world.

### Xiazi · Yesterday's World

I have always been intensely curious about the world.

AI, technology, business, culture, sport, design…

An enormous number of things happen every day.

What we often lack is not more information, but the ability to:

> Reduce it, choose the eight hottest stories, and show visually what they actually mean.

That became Xiazi.

It reorganizes the world's daily news into stories that are clear, visual, and have a point of view.

It combines content, design, and my ongoing observation of the world.

### Style Atlas

This is a product about visual styles, art, and learning design—made to help more people develop their aesthetic judgment.

After many years in design, I have come to believe that what matters is not memorizing the names of styles, but training one ability:

> Seeing.

Why does one image feel comfortable?

Why does another composition feel powerful?

What is happening with color, proportion, rhythm, negative space, and visual focus?

What we call “taste” is not necessarily a mysterious gift.

It can be observed, analyzed, and slowly trained.

### Brand & Growth Design

WonderElian also holds my professional work.

I do not want to set “work” against “personal creation.”

This is my most honest design training ground right now.

Brand strategy, websites, brochures, advertising, exhibitions, product visuals…

Every day, these projects make me confront a real commercial question:

> How can design genuinely help a product be understood, trusted, and chosen?

They also document my gradual movement from “visual designer” toward brand design.

### WonderElian OPS

As I made more things, a new question appeared:

> How do I manage and operate them?

Projects, data, content, experiments, operations, ideas, and next actions began to scatter across different places.

So I built myself an AI-powered automated operations system.

It is not designed to turn life into KPIs.

Quite the opposite.

I want the system to take over repetitive, trivial, automatable work, leaving me more time for the things that truly require judgment, taste, and creativity.

This is also how I understand AI today:

> Not as a way to make people more like machines, but as a way for machines to carry more of the work machines should do.

![Seemingly separate paths are joining into one river.](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-05.jpg)

## CHAPTER 06｜These Things Look Scattered, but They Have Always Been the Same Work

Friends sometimes ask:

> What exactly are you doing?

Meditation, Human Design, the Tao Te Ching, art styles, industrial branding, AI systems…

Isn't it all too scattered?

I used to worry about that too.

I felt that a person needed a perfectly clear label:

Designer.

Entrepreneur.

AI creator.

Product manager.

Blogger.

Over time, I realized that perhaps I do not need one.

The subjects may be different, but the way I approach them is remarkably consistent.

With an industrial machine, I ask how complex technology can be explained clearly.

With the Tao Te Ching, I ask how ancient words can re-enter modern life.

With Human Design, I ask how a complex system can become a visual structure ordinary people can understand.

With news, I ask what deserves to be seen in an immense flow of information.

With art, I ask how a vague “feeling” can become a visual language that can be learned.

If I had to name the common thread now, I would say:

> I like to reorganize things that are complex, abstract, or cold, then use design, AI, and products to make them clear, beautiful, and warm.

Design is my language.

AI is a new tool.

Products are how ideas become real.

And curiosity is probably the force behind it all.

## CHAPTER 07｜I Still Feel Anxious. I Just No Longer Demand an Answer to Life

Turning 40 did not suddenly make me perfectly clear-minded.

I still have pressure at work.

A mortgage.

A child.

I still worry about the future.

I still wonder what would happen if my job disappeared one day.

When I see other people succeed as entrepreneurs, I still feel envy.

As AI develops faster and faster, I still wonder whether my abilities might one day stop mattering.

None of these questions has disappeared.

What has changed is this:

> I no longer demand that I understand the next ten years of my life today.

In the past, anxiety made me rush to find a “second growth curve.”

Now I would rather do my current work well, deepen my brand-design practice, and use evenings and weekends to make the ideas that genuinely create a response in me.

I am not rushing to monetize everything immediately.

But I am not simply playing without direction either.

With every product, I hope to leave something behind:

A body of work.

A method.

A new capability.

A real experience.

Or simply a deeper understanding of myself.

Take it slowly.

See where these things eventually lead me.

## CHAPTER 08｜From “Proving Myself” to “Becoming Myself”

If I were to summarize the first forty years of my life, I would divide them into two stages.

In the first half, I kept learning:

> How to become a more impressive person.

In the second half, I want to learn:

> How to become myself.

That does not mean giving up effort.

Nor does it mean lying flat.

On the contrary, I still design, experiment with AI, build products, work, and support my family every day. I still want a better income and more choices.

What has changed is the motive behind the effort.

Before, it was:

> I need to prove that I can.

Now, it is closer to:

> I genuinely want to do this, so I want to do it well.

The two may look similar from the outside.

But they feel completely different in the body.

![You do not have to be complete to keep moving.](/assets/notes/2026-08-15-proving-to-becoming/image-06.jpg)

## CHAPTER 09｜WonderElian May Stay with Me for a Long Time

I do not know what WonderElian will eventually become.

Perhaps it will remain a personal website.

Perhaps some of its products will slowly grow.

Perhaps something I cannot imagine today will appear in the future.

That is all right.

I hope it always keeps a little “Wonder.”

Curiosity.

Surprise.

Miracle.

An interest in the world.

And a willingness to keep making things.

The name Elian carries a private meaning for me:

> I hope I can “live as a ray of light.”

When I was younger, I thought light meant brilliance, success, and being seen by many people.

My understanding has changed.

Light does not have to be dazzling.

It can simply mean:

Making one thing with care.

Offering a little help when someone needs it.

Explaining something complex clearly.

Being kinder to my family.

Being kinder to myself.

And after living through darkness, still choosing to believe that beauty exists in life.

WonderElian therefore has no grand ultimate mission.

It simply records how a 40-year-old designer continues to use design to understand the world, uses AI to make things that genuinely interest him, and learns again how to live.

> Know yourself within.
Move like water through the world.
Then, slowly, become yourself.
